title: Reverse an array in-place (two-pointer swap from ends).
keyPoints: Put one pointer at each end, swap the two elements, step both inward, and stop when they meet.
The loop runs n/2 times and uses only one temporary variable, giving O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
Use strict less-than (left < right) as the stopping condition so the middle element in odd-length arrays stays in place.
In-place reversal mutates the caller's array, which is an API side effect that must be documented.
Provide both a mutating in-place method and a non-mutating copy method so callers can choose.
This two-pointer swap is a building block for rotation, palindrome checking, and the next-permutation algorithm.

s1_definition.oneliner: Put one pointer at each end, swap, step both inward, and stop when they meet.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Two pointers** – `left` starts at index 0, `right` starts at the last index.
- **Swap and step** – exchange the two elements, then `left++` and `right--`.
- **Stop condition** – loop while `left < right`; strict less-than handles odd-length arrays cleanly.
- **O(n) time** – n/2 swaps, each constant time.
- **O(1) space** – only one temporary variable for the swap; no second array allocated.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India has Rajesh's transaction history listed oldest first, but the mobile app must show newest first. Rather than copying into a second list, two clerks start at opposite ends of the same list, swap the two entries they are holding, then each take one step toward the middle and swap again, continuing until they meet in the centre.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Reversing an array in place uses the two-pointer technique. I put one index at the start and one at the end, and while the left index is strictly less than the right I swap the two elements, then step both inward. When they meet, the array is reversed in linear time with constant extra space.

The detail I always get right is the stopping condition: strict less-than ensures the middle element in an odd-length array stays in place without a wasted self-swap.

The API decision I highlight is mutation versus copy. In-place reversal changes the caller's array, which is efficient but a side effect. I document the mutation and provide a separate method that returns a reversed copy when the original must be preserved.

In my banking project at National Bank of India, I used this to present Rajesh's transaction references newest first on the mobile activity screen, where the stored order is oldest first.

Remember one sentence: two pointers at the ends, swap and step inward while left is strictly less than right, and document the mutation.
